title: Motor base shuts off mid-blend
shortDescription: Thermal protection engaged after long or heavy blending.
fullDescription:
NutriBullet Pro 900 and Rx motor bases include a thermal cutout. After ~60 seconds of continuous blending with heavy ingredients, the motor stops to protect itself.

Allow the base to cool for 15-30 minutes before restarting.

fixSteps.title: Blend in pulses
fixSteps.instruction: Use 15-second bursts instead of continuous run.

whenToCallPro: If unit does not restart after 1 hour cool-down.
videoSearchQuery: NutriBullet Pro wont turn on overheated

faq.a: Yes, exceed and thermal cutout triggers.

title: Blade assembly seized
shortDescription: Dried residue or ice block preventing rotation.
fullDescription:
If the blade does not spin when locked to the base, debris may have dried inside the blade hub, or ice has jammed the vanes.

Rinse the extractor blade thoroughly and run hot water over the bearing area.

fixSteps.title: Soak in hot water
fixSteps.instruction: Submerge blade in hot soapy water 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Verify free spin
fixSteps.instruction: Blade should rotate smoothly by hand after cleaning.

faq.a: No — sealed unit, replace if bearing fails.

title: Cup spins without motor activation
shortDescription: Cup lugs not seated into base drive.
fullDescription:
The NutriBullet cup must be twisted onto the base until the lugs engage the clutch. If the cup rotates freely, try pushing down firmly while twisting.

Inspect lugs for wear — worn lugs will slip.

fixSteps.title: Push and twist
fixSteps.instruction: Press cup firmly down while twisting clockwise.

fixSteps.title: Inspect lugs
fixSteps.instruction: Look at the three tabs on blade for rounded wear.

faq.a: Often fit but may wear fast.

title: Liquid leaking where blade meets cup
shortDescription: Worn gasket ring on blade assembly.
fullDescription:
A rubber gasket seals the blade to the cup. Over time it compresses or cracks, allowing liquid to leak onto the motor base.

Replace the gasket or entire blade assembly.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Remove blade and lift the black rubber ring.

fixSteps.title: Replace gasket
fixSteps.instruction: Install new gasket or blade assembly.

fixSteps.title: Dry motor base
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and dry thoroughly before use.

whenToCallPro: If motor base was soaked, do not reuse without test.

title: Motor emits burning odor
shortDescription: Brush or winding damage from overload.
fullDescription:
Brushed motors wear naturally, and a faint carbon smell after heavy use is normal. Persistent burning odor with smoke is not — indicates brush or winding damage.

Stop use immediately if smoke is visible.

fixSteps.title: Cool and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Leave 1 hour; look for melted plastic smell.

fixSteps.title: Warranty claim
fixSteps.instruction: NutriBullet warranty is 1 year; file claim.

title: Rx SouperBlast cycle ends before 7 minutes
fullDescription:
The NutriBullet Rx SouperBlast cycle runs for ~7 minutes to heat soups. If it stops early, the motor detected overload from oversized chunks or thick paste.

Restart with smaller, softer pieces.

fixSteps.title: Stay under fill line
fixSteps.instruction: Do not exceed MAX line on pitcher.

title: Motor base dead
shortDescription: Outlet, thermal fuse, or power cord issue.
fullDescription:
No motor activity at all may indicate a tripped thermal fuse (one-shot) inside the motor base after severe overheating, a failed cord, or a dead outlet.

Thermal fuse replacement is an intermediate DIY repair but voids warranty.

fixSteps.title: Cool 2 hours
fixSteps.instruction: If recently overheated, wait longer than usual.

faq.a: Yes but requires disassembly and soldering.

title: Blade wobbles or unit shakes badly
shortDescription: Worn blade bearing or bent shaft.
fullDescription:
Excessive vibration indicates bearing wear inside the blade assembly or a bent blade shaft, often from blending metal or bone pieces.

Replace the extractor blade — shaft is not user-serviceable.

fixSteps.title: Inspect blade
fixSteps.instruction: Spin blade by hand — should be smooth.
